governance_context.executive_summary: Build part of the ARC genomics application, a scientist-facing app within Syngenta's larger platform, and deliver QA test automation across four sequential milestones (P1 Foundation, P2a Services and Data, P2b Application Surface, P3 Launch). The stack includes a micro-frontend shell and ARC micro-frontend (React/Next.js), FastAPI and nomenclature services, Azure AD/MSAL authentication, and Snowflake, tested with Playwright, Jest, React Testing Library and Pytest. Syngenta owns the platform infrastructure and data tier, while Toptal owns ARC application development and automated testing of both Toptal-built and designated Syngenta-built components.

charter.project_purpose: Deliver the ARC application, which lets scientists search and view genomics association results and haplotype data, together with automated QA coverage across the ARC program.
delivery_objectives: Build the micro-frontend shell with global navigation, routing, shared design system and Azure AD/MSAL authentication.
Build FastAPI search, detail and asynchronous query services, plus the OneGWAS direct-write integration, over Snowflake ARC tables.
Build the ARC micro-frontend with faceted search, result detail, haplotype interval visualization and the nomenclature service.
Deliver automated test scripts, execution and defect reports across all four milestones, including integration, performance, security and cross-browser testing.
Run UAT after each milestone, complete a pre-launch hardening iteration, and perform production smoke tests with a 48-hour defect watch.
success_criteria: Each milestone passes its own acceptance review and client sign-off within a 5-business-day acceptance period.
Search performance meets targets of P95 under 1 second (P50 under 300ms, P90 under 700ms), with detail P95 under 500ms.
Authentication success is 100%, with token acquisition P95 under 800ms and silent token refresh working.
UAT exits with no open critical defects in Toptal-built work, and all critical and high defects are closed before cutover.
Production smoke tests pass 100% and the 48-hour defect watch is clean.
Frontend unit test coverage is at least 80%, and Chrome and Edge are validated.

A milestone acceptance review runs at the end of each milestone, and the client is asked to confirm each weekly status report.

commercial_guardrails.contract_type_implication: Fixed Fee with milestone billing, so Toptal carries the cost risk of overruns inside the defined scope. Anything outside that scope or the stated assumptions needs a Change Order, or margin is lost.
commercial_guardrails.billing_consumption_assumption: Each milestone fee is invoiced only when the milestone is completed, and Client is notified in writing if the actual date differs from the estimate. Client has 5 business days to accept or reject, and silence or production use counts as acceptance. Billing is not driven by timesheets.
commercial_guardrails.staffing_assumption: Toptal staffs ARC application development (shell, micro-frontend, FastAPI services, nomenclature service) and all QA test automation, with Delivery Manager Saadia Iqbal. Toptal work cannot start until the related Client-built work, personnel and environments are ready, and no holiday stoppages are assumed. Team size and hours are not specified.
commercial_guardrails.commercial_exposure_note: Exposure comes from heavy Client dependencies, the sequential milestone gates, and UAT being included in the fixed fee. Open points that could erode margin are no design/UX role assigned, an undefined number of ARC-specific design components, and the start date and holiday assumptions. Client delays, untrue assumptions or a talent buyout excuse Toptal from delays but may not automatically adjust fees.
commercial_guardrails.approved_work_rule: Only the Work Output defined for the four milestones (P1 Foundation, P2a Services and Data, P2b Application Surface, P3 Launch) and any agreed Change Orders may be executed. This includes up to two UAT runs per milestone, one re-execution of Certification tests after Client remediation, and the 48-hour post-deployment defect watch.
commercial_guardrails.non_approved_work_rule: The following need a Change Order before work starts: a third or later UAT run, additional test re-runs, rework from upstream Snowflake schema or API taxonomy changes, design-system changes or extra components, and testing of Client-built items not listed. Also excluded are remediation of Client-built defects, hypercare beyond the 48-hour watch, post-launch maintenance and design-system maintenance.
commercial_guardrails.work_at_risk_rule: No work-at-risk provision is defined. Any work started before a Change Order is agreed or outside milestone scope requires written PMO Lead approval and executive exception sign-off.
commercial_guardrails.change_control_trigger: A Change Order is triggered by changes that significantly affect scope, timeline or cost, by assumptions found untrue or incomplete, and by Cogen availability below about 95%. Other triggers are UAT beyond two runs per milestone, design-system changes, and extra test cycles driven by Client-side changes. A mutually agreed start-date shift does not need one.
commercial_guardrails.change_order_route: The Toptal Delivery Manager and Client Contact (Mike Magwire) raise the change in writing and negotiate an equitable fee and schedule adjustment in good faith. The change takes effect once both parties agree to the Change Order in writing.
commercial_guardrails.budget_baseline: Total Fixed Fee of $200,365: Milestone 1 $26,808, Milestone 2 $60,356, Milestone 3 $68,210, Milestone 4 $44,991.
commercial_guardrails.variance_indicator: Green at baseline: work has not started (estimated start October 7, 2026) and no variance is recorded.
commercial_guardrails.escalation_threshold: No numeric threshold is defined. Escalate any estimated milestone date slip, Client dependency delay or Change Order trigger to the PMO Lead. Unresolved disputes follow three levels: Delivery Manager and Client Contact, then their managers (5 business days each), then executives.

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Schedule: "Estimated Start Date October 7, 2026" and fixed milestone dates from Nov 17, 2026 to Apr 6, 2027. Internal scope notes: "No date has been agreed with Syngenta, and the phase sequence hangs off it."
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: All four milestone dates and billing dates depend on a start date that may not be confirmed, creating schedule and cash-flow risk. The start date is also the same day the agreement takes effect.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: Can Client confirm in writing that October 7, 2026 is the agreed start date, with Client onboarding items (access, design system, standards) ready by then?

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Assumptions: "The schedule and cost were created considering that no breaks or stoppages due to holidays will occur." The 26-week plan from Oct 7, 2026 to Apr 6, 2027 spans Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year.
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: Holiday shutdowns on either side are unaccounted for and could push milestone dates without a clear right to adjust the schedule or fees.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: Will Client confirm that no holiday or shutdown periods apply, or agree an adjusted calendar and the treatment of Client-side unavailability?

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Assumptions: milestones run sequentially as acceptance gates, with P2b starting "upon acceptance of P2a" and P3 "upon acceptance of P2b". UAT runs after each milestone. Acceptance: 5 business days for review. Schedule: fixed back-to-back week ranges (1–6, 7–16, 17–21, 22–26) with no time for review, UAT or rework between gates.
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: Acceptance periods, two UAT runs and rework between gates are not built into the fixed week ranges, so any slippage in Client review delays all later milestones.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: Is the acceptance and UAT time for each milestone inside or outside the stated week ranges, and does the next milestone start only after formal acceptance?

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Acceptance: a criterion "(including one expressed as 100%) is deemed satisfied if the Work Output materially conforms… and any deviation does not materially affect its functionality, performance, security, or usability." Exhibit A criteria include "Authentication success 100%" and "100% critical-path pass".
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: Numeric targets can be read as absolute or as material-conformance, which invites disputes about milestone acceptance and the invoice. Rejection tests such as "within Client's reasonable discretion" are subjective.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: Will Client confirm in writing that the materiality standard applies to all numeric and 100% criteria, and define how "material" and "reasonable discretion" are assessed?

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Acceptance: deemed acceptance after 5 business days of silence, yet "Client will sign and deliver… a certification of milestone acceptance". Fees: invoiced "upon completion of the milestone". Client Contact is Mike Magwire only; internal notes say sign-off comes from "Mike Magwire and Satya".
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: It is unclear whether invoicing follows completion, deemed acceptance or signed certification, and who the authorized approvers are. This risks delayed or disputed milestone payments.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: Who are the named approvers for each milestone, and is the invoice triggered at completion notice, deemed acceptance or signed certification?

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Activities: Toptal will "Build automated pipeline quality gates and deployment smoke checks (HS-4770)". Work Output: HS-4770 is typed "Certification", meaning a Client-built component that Toptal only tests. CI/CD pipelines (HS-4768) are Client-owned and out of scope for Toptal.
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: It is unclear whether Toptal builds the quality gates or only tests Client-built ones, which affects effort, acceptance and responsibility for failures.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: Does Toptal build the HS-4770 gates and smoke checks inside Client's pipeline, or only write and run tests against gates Client builds?

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: QA principles: "Testing ARC means testing against the full platform. SSO and the external integrations are within the test scope." Assumptions: "Testing of other Client-built components, pipelines or environments is not included and may be added by Change Order."
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: The test boundary is unclear. Full-platform testing could expand effort beyond the fixed fee, or Client could expect broader coverage than the listed deliverables.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: Is test scope limited to the listed test deliverables, or does it cover all platform components touched by ARC flows? If the latter, please list those components.

source_reference.document_name: Syngenta Crop Protection, LLC - ARC Application Implementation SOW + Exhibit A.pdf

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: QA principles: failures in Client-built components are Client's to fix, and Toptal re-executes tests "in accordance with the Assumptions"; "Additional re-runs will be addressed by Change Order." Internal notes: "the remediation path has not been written down."
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: No agreed number of free re-tests, response times or escalation path for Client-owned failures. Retests and idle time could erode margin and delay milestone acceptance.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: How many re-test cycles are included per Certification item, within what timeframe must Client remediate, and what happens to the milestone date if remediation is late?

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Latency criteria: a missed target is treated as met if telemetry "may show" it is attributable to a Client-owned component or environmental conditions. Search P95 < 1s is fixed in milestone 2, while HS-4942 (same milestone) is where "p95 targets defined" and observability is built.
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: Latency acceptance depends on a subjective attribution finding and on observability delivered in the same milestone. Client could dispute a "met" finding, or targets could be redefined after commitment.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: Who decides whether a latency miss is attributable to Client-owned components, on what evidence, and are the listed P95 targets final or subject to revision after HS-4942?

contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: "Approximately 95%" has no measurement window or method, and provisioning of Cogen and Tagasys is unconfirmed. Test failures and retest cycles could become disputed Change Orders.

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Assumptions: UAT is included in the fixed price, "limited to two (2) runs per Milestone, covering all UAT and not only Toptal-built Work". P3 acceptance requires "no open critical defects in Toptal-built Work at exit", and UAT coordination and sign-off (HS-4827) is Client's. Internal notes: UAT scope boundaries and change-order triggers are "not yet written".
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: Two runs may not close critical defects, including those in Client-built work. This risks Change Orders, a delayed P3 exit and disputes over who bears extra cycles.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: What is a UAT "run" (duration, scope, retest rules), and what happens to P3 exit if criticals remain open after two runs?

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Acceptance: "48-hour defect watch clean" (HS-4832) and "legacy traffic = 0 over watch window" (HS-4788), with no definition of "clean" or the watch window. Hypercare beyond the 48-hour watch is out of scope (HS-4944).
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: Post-launch acceptance has no objective threshold and no stated remediation obligation after cutover, so Client may expect fixes or extended monitoring within the fixed fee.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: What defines a "clean" defect watch (severity thresholds), how long is the HS-4788 watch window, and who fixes defects found during the 48 hours?

contract_ambiguities.conflicting_clauses: Acceptance: "Long queries offloaded" via an async task queue (HS-4778) on a platform targeting sub-second search P95 < 1s; no threshold defines "long". Training deliverable (HS-4829) is accepted when "delivered and reviewed", with no audience, format or volume defined, although training is otherwise out of scope.
contract_ambiguities.risk_impact: Without a threshold for "long" queries, acceptance of the async work is subjective and its necessity unclear. Undefined training content invites scope growth under a fixed fee.
contract_ambiguities.recommended_clarification: What query duration qualifies as "long-running", and what are the exact training audience, format, quantity and review criteria for HS-4829?
